comments.body:
SEAM ANALYSIS COMPLETE — a decided split, with the test-seam risk checked per member. This resolves
this ticket's Approach from "candidate" to a concrete plan.

RECOMMENDED ORDER, and why this order:

1) gate_dispatch.py (799) -> extract the PLAN-REVIEW RECOVERY cluster into a new
   src/rebar/llm/workflow/plan_review_recovery.py (~300 LOC). gate_dispatch lands at ~518.
   Members: the STEP_* constants + _PLAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED_STEP_IDS (:51-68), GateContractError
   (:71-75), _collect_step_ids (:78-91), _validate_gate_step_ids (:94-108), _DET_STEP_IDS/
   _LLM_STEP_KINDS (:243-246), _attach_plan_review_metrics (:249-334),
   _recover_plan_review_coach_failure (:337-380), _recover_plan_review_verify_failure (:383-444),
   _degraded_plan_review_verdict (:447-480).
   The cluster is REAL, not carved: _validate_gate_step_ids calls _collect_step_ids; all three
   reconstruction functions key off the STEP_* ids; the file's own comment at :51-57 says the
   constants exist FOR the recovery/metrics logic. Only produce_plan_review_verdict calls in, and
   only at the cluster's top edge — no mid-cluster entry.
   WHY FIRST: it is the only candidate with ZERO string-monkeypatched members, AND it carries all
   THREE of gate_dispatch's five finalize_verdict call sites (:377, :441, :478) into a module with
   ~500 lines of headroom — which is precisely what unblocks 343b's gap-5 wiring.

2) orchestrator.py (796) -> extract the run-scoped CONTEXT-ASSEMBLY cluster (:88-244, ~157 LOC) into
   src/rebar/llm/plan_review/context_assembly.py. orchestrator lands at ~641, leaving finalize_verdict
   in place with ~160 lines of room for 343b's parameter.
   Members: _assemble_cache, assemble_context_cache, _assemble_cache_key, assemble_context,
   _assemble_context_uncached. One purpose: read the ticket graph once per gate run and memoize it.

3) DO NOT extract the code-review gate cluster (:481-729) in this ticket. code_review_enabled is
   monkeypatched BY STRING on the gate_dispatch module object at 14 sites, and its sole internal
   caller _code_review_preflight would move with it — so the moved caller would read the NEW module's
   binding and all 14 patches would silently stop taking effect. Making it work requires converting
   that reference to a module-attribute lookup, which is a DESIGN CHANGE, not a relocation, and must
   not be smuggled into a size-driven split. Separate ticket.

ZERO-TEST-EDIT MECHANISM (the 2682/3a98 precedent): re-import the moved names back into the origin
module so they remain ITS module-globals. Verified for every Seam-B member — all external references
are either `from ... import X` or `gate_dispatch.X` attribute access, both of which survive a
re-import. Includes pytest.raises(gate_dispatch.GateContractError), which holds because it is the
same class object.

TWO LOAD-BEARING CAUTIONS FOUND IN THE ANALYSIS:
- PRESERVE THE REFERENCE STYLE. The recovery functions reach orchestrator via a lazy
  `from rebar.llm.plan_review import orchestrator` then ATTRIBUTE access (orchestrator.finalize_verdict
  etc.). tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_execution_floor_lifecycle.py:85 monkeypatches
  orchestrator.pass3_over_findings and then calls the recovery function. Flattening to
  `from ...orchestrator import pass3_over_findings` would silently break that patch. Move the code
  VERBATIM.
- MOVE THE STEP_* CONSTANTS WITH THE CLUSTER rather than leaving them behind. Leaving them creates a
  genuine module-level cycle; the alternative (mirroring the strings locally, as
  code_review/finalize.py:22-27 already does) would create a THIRD copy of those strings, and
  finalize.py:14-15 already carries a "must be mirrored" warning. Single source of truth is both
  safer and cheaper here.

IMPORT-CYCLE CHECKS (both clean, no TYPE_CHECKING guard needed):
- plan_review_recovery.py needs only `from __future__ import annotations` + typing.Any at module
  level; every other import is already lazy inside the moved bodies. One-way edge
  gate_dispatch -> plan_review_recovery, mirroring code_review/finalize.py's posture.
- context_assembly.py imports only siblings/leaves (det_floor, sizing, config), none of which import
  orchestrator. NOTE production_batch_runner.py:49 does `from .orchestrator import assemble_context,
  route_criteria`, so the re-import into orchestrator is LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic.

# The 800-LOC cap is saturated: nine modules within 20 lines, three exactly at it

## Measured (this worktree, rebased on current origin/main)

| file | LOC | headroom |
|---|---|---|
| `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py` | **800** | **0** |
| `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` | **800** | **0** |
| `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py` | **800** | **0** |
| `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` | 799 | 1 |
| `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` | 796 | 4 |
| `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` | 793 | 7 |
| `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py` | 791 | 9 |
| `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py` | 787 | 13 |
| `src/rebar/_store/event_append.py` | 782 | 18 |

## Why this is a blocker, not an observation

It is already blocking real work. Story 343b's remaining gap (the gate verdict must carry
`provider_provenance`; see that ticket's "gap 5") requires threading one value through
`orchestrator.finalize_verdict` and its FIVE call sites, which live in `orchestrator.py` (4 lines
of headroom), `workflow_ops.py` (13) and `gate_dispatch.py` (**1 line**, with THREE of the five
call sites). The minimal possible change — one helper, one defaulted parameter, one added key, one
argument per call site — cannot fit. Even folding the helper into a roomy module leaves
`gate_dispatch.py` needing +3 lines against 1 line of headroom, and the kwarg cannot be appended to
the existing lines without breaching the 100-char E501 limit.

So a correct, minimal, well-tested change is physically unlandable until something is split.

## This is the third instance in one epic

- `runner.py` hit 800 during story dc0d -> task 2682 split it.
- `runner.py` hit it AGAIN after main grew it to 798 -> ticket 3a98 split it further.
- `attest.py` was at 799 and a two-call-site kwarg change only fit by importing a function directly
  to dodge an E501 wrap, landing at EXACTLY 800 -> ticket c6c9 filed to split it, still open.
Each was treated as a one-off. Nine modules at the edge says it is not.

## The cost is not only structural

The cap is now shaping documentation and design quality, not just file layout:
- In `attest.py` the explanatory comments for a security-relevant change had to be cut to a pointer
  purely to save lines.
- Here, the natural home for the cfg->record helper is beside its consumer; it has to go elsewhere
  purely for space, which is the "split mechanically to hit a number" the module-size policy itself
  forbids.
- The next person to fix a one-line bug in any of the nine pays an unrelated refactor first, under
  whatever time pressure that bug carries.

## Approach (candidate, deliberately not a decision)

Do NOT raise the limit — it is locked, and an administrator override is the documented path for a
limit change precisely so this stays deliberate. Instead, treat the saturated set as a queue and
split along seams that ALREADY exist in the call graph, one module at a time, as 2682 and 3a98 did.
Both of those are worked precedents: 2682 extracted the structured-run cluster with ZERO test edits;
3a98 moved the pai preflight cluster into it, also with zero test edits, by re-importing the moved
names so existing monkeypatch seams kept resolving.

Priority should follow what is BLOCKING rather than what is largest: `gate_dispatch.py` (1 line,
blocking 343b today), then `orchestrator.py` (4), then the three at exactly 800.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` is under 700 LOC, split along an existing call-graph
      seam, with zero test edits or each edit justified in the commit message
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py` is under 700 LOC on the same terms
- [ ] no extracted module is under 100 LOC (the anti-fragmentation floor)
- [ ] after the split, `gate_dispatch.py` has at least 100 lines of headroom under the 800-LOC cap,
      reported as the before/after LOC in the commit message. This is the ticket's PURPOSE stated
      observably: 343b must add one argument at each of the three `finalize_verdict` call sites that
      live in that file, which is unlandable against the 1 line of headroom it has today. This ticket
      does NOT perform that wiring — it only makes it landable, and the wiring is asserted by 343b.
- [ ] [operator-attested] the full suite passes with a test count equal to the pre-split count plus
      any new seam tests, evidenced by the two pytest summary lines in a comment
compiled_state.title: Split the modules saturating the 800-LOC cap, starting with gate_dispatch
